pr_title: apps.c: re-enable loading single certs and CRLs over HTTP
pr_comments:
> It's a shame we can't think of an easy way to test this...but I can see it would be difficult.

Yeah. This was also a major problem during the submission of #11998.
As mentioned, I solved this by `test/recipes/81-test_cmp_cli.t` calling `apps/cmp.c` with the option `-port`,
which runs a rudimentary HTTP server based on `apps/lib/http_server.c`.

Also further tests involving HTTP clients and servers could do something similar.

The two recently reported CI failures
```
ssl/ssl_lib.c: In function 'SSL_set0_tmp_dh_pkey':
ssl/ssl_lib.c:5963:9: error: implicit declaration of function 'SSLerr' [-Werror=implicit-function-declaration]
         SSLerr(0, SSL_R_DH_KEY_TOO_SMALL);
```
are unrelated.

Rebasing (and squashing on this occasion) in the hope that this spurious issue goes away.

issue_context.title: HTTP CRL downloading broken in master
issue_context.body:
s_client and s_server have the ability to automatically download CRLs for certificates that they receive and immediately check their revocation status. This works just fine in 1.1.1

Here is an example of this working in 1.1.1

Start s_server:
````
$ openssl s_server -cert testcert.pem -key private.key
````

Start your favourite lightweight http server:
````
$ http-server -p 8080
````

Finally start s_client:
````
$ openssl s_client -CAfile .rootCA.pem -verify_return_error -crl_check -crl_download
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 C = AU, ST = Some-State, O = Internet Widgits Pty Ltd
verify error:num=23:certificate revoked
140002436080960:error:1416F086:SSL routines:tls_process_server_certificate:certificate verify failed:ssl/statem/statem_clnt.c:1913:
---
no peer certificate available
---
No client certificate CA names sent
Server Temp Key: X25519, 253 bits
---
SSL handshake has read 1182 bytes and written 318 bytes
Verification error: certificate revoked
---
New, TLSv1.3, Cipher is TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
Secure Renegotiation IS NOT supported
Compression: NONE
Expansion: NONE
No ALPN negotiated
Early data was not sent
Verify return code: 23 (certificate revoked)
---
````

As you can see this successfully detects that the certificate is revoked and aborts the connection.

On master we instead see:
````
$ openssl s_client -CAfile ../test/certs/rootCA.pem -verify_return_error -crl_check -crl_download
CONNECTED(00000003)
Could not open file or uri for loading CRL via CDP from http://127.0.0.1:8080/crl.der
80A2A68A207F0000:error::STORE routines:ossl_store_get0_loader_int:unregistered scheme:crypto/store/store_register.c:240:scheme=http
Unable to load CRL via CDP
depth=0 C = AU, ST = Some-State, O = Internet Widgits Pty Ltd
verify error:num=3:unable to get certificate CRL
80A2A68A207F0000:error::SSL routines:tls_process_server_certificate:certificate verify failed:ssl/statem/statem_clnt.c:1857:
---
no peer certificate available
---
No client certificate CA names sent
Server Temp Key: X25519, 253 bits
---
SSL handshake has read 1182 bytes and written 322 bytes
Verification error: unable to get certificate CRL
---
New, TLSv1.3, Cipher is TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
Secure Renegotiation IS NOT supported
Compression: NONE
Expansion: NONE
No ALPN negotiated
Early data was not sent
Verify return code: 3 (unable to get certificate CRL)
---
````

This seems to have been introduced by commit 6d382c74.

comments: Hmmm, I may have a fix lying around.

Oops, when doing commit 6d382c7 I must have wrongly assumed that OSSL_STORE would handle http.
This should be fixed by #13404 (though I did not bother setting up an HTTP server for testing it).
BTW, would be nice if there was an automatic test for the case outlined by @mattcaswell above.

> BTW, would be nice if there was an automatic test for the case outlined by @mattcaswell above.

Hmmm...  that would require setting up a light http server for tests.  I believe there are perl libraries that do this, but that would rely on non-core perl modules...

Yep, that's not trivial.
`test/recipes/81-test_cmp_cli.t` does that via `apps/cmp.c` which, when called with the `-port` option, 
runs a rudimentary HTTP server based on `apps/lib/http_server.c`.

review_comments: Oh, it was that simple???  Ok then!

Yes - everything needed is still there, even with more flexibility.
For instance, one could give a timeout value and custom BIOs.
HTTP redirection etc. is now also supported under the hood.
